Attacks can deal Slash, Pierce, Blunt, Fire, Frost, Lightning, Poison, or Arcane damage. Monsters have different levels of resistance to these damage types.

Try different attacks to learn what works best. A monster's resistance to a given type of damage is automatically registered on their entry on the diary.

People have different affinities with weapons, which in turn dictate what weapons they are capable of using.

The weapons available to each individual can be altered by learning a different class.

Strength supports physical attacks, while Mental Acuity supports mental abilities.

Defense reduces damage from attacks that test physical defenses; Mental Resilience reduces damage from those that test mental defenses.

Each ability determines which stats it uses. Elemental damage types tend to be associated with mental damage, but there are exceptions.

Explorers may equip one weapon and carry 4 pieces of gear. Out of those four, they may only equip up to 3 artifacts, up to one medallion and up to one consumable.

They can equip up to three Artifacts, one Medallion, and one Consumable, within that total.

Artifacts modify stats and affinities.

Medallions grant abilities while equipped.

Consumables can heal, strengthen allies, harm enemies, or weaken them; their uses are limited.

Buffs temporarily strengthen a unit, while debuffs weaken it. Other status effects can cause ongoing damage or prevent actions.

Check a character’s Overview to see active effects and their remaining turns.

Choose your abilities wisely to inflice the status you need.

Every weapon family has its own focus. Individual designs may vary.

Guns
Great damage and great Speed, suited to fast physical offense.

Crossbows
Focus on damage, with some Speed and a modest boost to Mental Acuity.

Daggers
Specialize in Speed, favoring quick attacks over heavy blows.

Amplifiers
Specialize in Mental Acuity, strengthening mental offense.

Swords
Balance physical damage and Speed, making them versatile weapons.

Hammers
Favor powerful physical damage at the expense of Speed.

Spears
Balance physical damage with Defense, favoring a steadier approach.

Visit the Tinkerer to commission weapons and medallions from their available designs.

Accept a commission before setting out: defeating the requested monsters automatically gathers the materials for it. Kills made before accepting the commission do not count.

Return to the Tinkerer when the requirements are met to collect the finished item. A design they have never fabricated needs more materials than one they have made before.

Your new equipment enters the shared stash; equip it from the character’s Gear tab.

Sleep at the barracks to restore the whole party’s health and SP, including companions in reserve.

Experience gained in battle takes effect when you sleep.

If a character has earned enough experience to level up, you can review their progress and any newly learned abilities before waking.

Sleeping does not replenish consumable uses, so check your supplies before leaving.

Toggle Observe while choosing a character’s action in battle to help them learn more from the encounter.

While observing, that character earns more experience, but their Strength, Defense, Mental Acuity, Mental Resilience, and Speed are greatly reduced.

Once switched on, the effects of Observe are maintained until ends when the battle ends or the option is switched off.

Use Observe when you need a big boost in experience for an explorer.

Map completion represents how much of the current labyrinth you have charted. Walk through uncharted rooms to increase it.

You can check your progress in the book’s Map section and labryinths are recreated every time you enter them, so the completion is reset every time.

The party remembers its highest completion reached in a single visit since its last sleep.

Be sure to explore as much as you can to ensure efficient growth.
